assertions.text: List values in the table use bracket syntax like [tech:java, biz:sales, dev:ci] — not comma-separated strings without brackets.
Empty list input uses [] (not a blank cell, which represents null). The distinction between empty list and null is preserved.
assertions.evidence: "empty list                  | []" and blank cells for null requiredCategories

assertions.text: Values containing pipes (|), brackets, or colons (:) are properly quoted (e.g. "tech:java") so they don't conflict with table syntax. Colons without quoting would be mis-interpreted as map key:value entries.

Set<String> values in the table use curly brace syntax like {tech, dev} — not bracket syntax [tech, dev] which is for lists. The distinction between Set and List types is preserved in the table notation.
Cell values containing newlines use \n escaping — not literal line breaks that would break the table row structure.
Values containing pipe characters (|) are quoted so they don't conflict with the markdown table column separator. For example, a tag like 'biz:hr|recruiting' must be quoted.
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: | Scenario                        | Tags | ... (first column in all three tables)

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Filtered tags?' or 'Result?')
assertions.evidence: | Filtered Tags? (appears in all three @TableTest tables)

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: assertEquals(filteredTags, subject.filterTags(...)) — only assertion, no conditionals

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest annotation present before methods, no @DisplayName or @Description

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotations present in the output
